title: Skill, Sequence, and Scoring
text:
Key Findings

1. Traditional scoring is sequence-sensitive
The order of frames matters. The same frame composition can produce a score range of up to 39 points under traditional scoring, while World Bowling collapses all orderings to a single score.
Try it yourself →


2. Traditional scoring has a compounding reward gradient
Each consecutive strike is worth more than the last. Under World Bowling, every strike is worth the same regardless of context.
Explore the gradient →


3. The crossover point is ~50% strike rate
Below 50% strike rate, World Bowling provides more score spread. Above it, traditional scoring provides 33% more spread at the professional level.


4. Within-tier discrimination matters most
Both systems separate recreational from professional players equally well. The critical difference is in separating two elite players who differ in their ability to sustain consecutive strikes.

title: Sequence Sensitivity Explorer
text:
Try these experiments
Experiment 1: Strike placement matters

Enter: X, X, X, X, X, 5/, 5/, 5/, 5/ — note both scores
Clear and enter: 5/, 5/, 5/, 5/, X, X, X, X, X — note the traditional score changes, World Bowling stays the same

Experiment 2: Consecutive vs scattered strikes

Enter: X, X, X, 5,4, 5,4, 5,4, 5,4, 5,4, 5,4
Clear and enter: X, 5,4, X, 5,4, X, 5,4, 5,4, 5,4, 5,4
Same three strikes, but consecutive strikes score higher under traditional scoring

Experiment 3: The commutativity proof in action

Enter any 9 frames you like and note the World Bowling score
Rearrange them in any order — the World Bowling score is always the same
This is Proposition 1 from the paper: World Bowling is commutative

title: Simulation Results
text:
Score Distributions by Tier
Notice how the distributions shift and compress differently under each system. At the recreational level, both systems produce similar shapes. At the professional level, World Bowling scores compress toward 300 while traditional scores maintain a wider spread.

title: Simulation Results
text:
The Crossover Point
The key finding: score spread crosses over at approximately 50% strike rate.

Below 50% (recreational, club): World Bowling provides more score spread. Its simplicity is a net benefit here.
Above 50% (elite, professional): Traditional scoring provides more spread — over 30% more at the Top 10 level.


The right panel shows the crossover clearly — the standard deviation lines cross between Competitive and Elite levels.

title: Simulation Results
text:
Robustness: Three Simulation Models
Does the finding hold if we make the simulation more realistic? We tested three models:

Independent — each ball is statistically independent (conservative baseline)
Momentum — strike probability shifts ±5% based on the previous frame
Markov chain + spare difficulty — state-dependent strike probabilities calibrated from PBA data, with leave-dependent spare conversion rates

All three models agree on the direction. More realistic models make the traditional scoring advantage larger, not smaller.

title: Simulation Results
text:
Professional-Level Sequences
At the professional level, specific game sequences show large score differences between the systems. The systems agree at the extremes (perfect game, all spares) but diverge substantially for the mixed sequences that make up real competitive bowling.

Key observation: “4 strikes then spares” scores 195 under traditional but 210 under World Bowling. “Spares then 4 strikes” scores 215 traditional but 210 World Bowling. Same frames, different order — traditional scoring encodes the difference, World Bowling erases it.

title: About
text:
Summary
This paper demonstrates, through exact combinatorial analysis and Monte Carlo simulation, that traditional and World Bowling scoring systems differ in mathematically precise and practically significant ways:

Traditional scoring is sequence-sensitive — the order of frames matters. World Bowling is commutative — order is irrelevant.
Traditional scoring has a compounding reward gradient — each consecutive strike is worth more. World Bowling is linear.
The scoring systems’ discriminating power crosses over at ~50% strike rate — below this, World Bowling provides more spread; above it, traditional provides 33% more at the professional level.
The distinction matters most within skill tiers — both systems separate recreational from professional players, but only traditional scoring separates elite players who differ in streak ability.
